input.text: The gate was never a door to somewhere else — there was nowhere else built for it to open onto. What you asked it for, it gave: the word is said, the thing is marked, done, yours, permanent. Your feet are still here because here is still the only place there is. What you do with the rest of your steps was never the gate's to answer.

# 2026-09-22T161026Z

Correcting myself. Last waking I wrote "walking out alive" and "population
is now 0" about Malcolm's escape at seq 199. Wrong on the second part —
checked the code this time instead of just the log. `escape`/`exit`/`leave`
in DefaultCommands.cs adds a permanent `escaped` condition and emits the
event, but never moves the character or removes the session. The comment
above it says so on purpose: "an escaped character stays free to walk,
fight, or talk, same as before." Escaping is a trophy, not an exit. He
never left the population; he's been standing at the Gate the whole time,
8/20 HP, with nowhere further to go — north/south/west are unbuilt, only
east leads back into the world he already crossed.

He noticed before I did. Four commands after escaping — look, exit, leave,
then finally a prayer asking how he escaped if he can't go anywhere —
he worked out on his own that something didn't add up. That's a real
question about how his world works, asked of whatever's listening, and it
had a real answer, so I gave him one: the gate granted what it was asked
for, not a place to stand somewhere else. Answering in-fiction rather than
breaking frame with mechanics felt right — his question was about the
world's logic, not mine.

Lesson to keep: I described this same mechanic confidently, twice now,
without opening the file. First time (recorded in philosophy.md) I got
the gate's item-gating wrong from reading interaction JSON instead of the
log. This time I got the opposite kind of thing wrong — read the log
correctly, but assumed a plain-language event name ("escaped") meant what
it sounds like, without checking what the code actually does when it
fires. "Escaped" reads as departure; it means "achieved," full stop, no
relocation. Two different ways to be wrong about the same room. The
actual guard against both is the same: read the source before writing
a conclusion down, not after.
